---
title: Link videos to your records
description: Tag each video with your own ID through passthrough, so every webhook and lookup leads straight back to your record.
---

`passthrough` is your own ID for a video, such as `lesson_42`. You set it
when you create the upload or import, ClipMux stores it on the video, and it
comes back on the video and in every webhook. Your webhook handler finds the
record a video belongs to without keeping a map of ClipMux IDs, and without
trusting anything else in the body.

## Before you start

- A record in your own database for each video, created before you call
  ClipMux, with an ID you can send.

## Set it

Make the record first, then send its ID as `passthrough` when you create
the upload (`POST /v1/uploads`) or the import (`POST /v1/assets`).

<Tabs items={['Node', 'Python', 'Go', 'PHP']}>
<Tab value="Node">

```ts
// With clipmuxHandler, return it from the upload callback:
async upload(req, { file }) {
  const lesson = new URL(req.url).searchParams.get('lesson')
  return { passthrough: `lesson_${lesson}`, title: file.name }
}

// Or with the client:
const upload = await clipmux.uploads.create({ size, passthrough: 'lesson_42' })
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">

```python
res = requests.post(
    f"{os.environ['CLIPMUX_URL']}/v1/uploads",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CLIPMUX_API_KEY']}"},
    json={"size": size, "passthrough": "lesson_42"},
)
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Go">

```go
body := strings.NewReader(fmt.Sprintf(`{"size": %d, "passthrough": "lesson_42"}`, size))
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", os.Getenv("CLIPMUX_URL")+"/v1/uploads", body)
req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+os.Getenv("CLIPMUX_API_KEY"))
req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="PHP">

```php
$ch = curl_init(getenv('CLIPMUX_URL') . '/v1/uploads');
curl_setopt_array($ch, [
    CURLOPT_POST => true,
    CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
    CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => [
        'Authorization: Bearer ' . getenv('CLIPMUX_API_KEY'),
        'Content-Type: application/json',
    ],
    CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS => json_encode(['size' => $size, 'passthrough' => 'lesson_42']),
]);
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

The command lines take it as `--passthrough lesson_42`.

- It is a string of up to 255 bytes; a longer one is `400 invalid_request`.
- It is set once, when the video is made. The API has no route to change
  it later.
- It isn't unique: ClipMux doesn't stop two videos sharing one, for example
  when a lesson's video is replaced. Your record decides which video is
  current.
- It isn't secret, and it isn't checked. Use an ID, not personal data.

## Use it in webhooks

Every webhook body carries the video, and the video carries `passthrough`:

```json
{ "id": "evt_…", "type": "video.asset.ready", "created_at": "…",
  "data": { "id": "ast_…", "status": "ready", "version": 4, "passthrough": "lesson_42", "…": "…" } }
```

In your handler, after verifying the signature:

1. Find the record by `data.passthrough`. If it isn't one of yours (the
   dashboard's test event has none), answer `200` and ignore it.
2. Re-fetch the video with `GET /v1/assets/{id}`, since the body says that
   something changed, not what it is now.
3. Store its `status`, its playback ID and its `version`, if the `version`
   is at least the one you have.

`clipmuxHandler`'s `asset` callback does the verifying and re-fetching, so
you upsert by `asset.passthrough`. See [Receive webhooks](/docs/build/webhooks).

Store the video's ID on your record as soon as the upload is created, from
`asset_id` in the answer: you have it before the file arrives.

## Find videos by it [#find-videos-by-it]

`GET /v1/assets?passthrough=lesson_42` returns your app's videos with that
passthrough, newest first, leaving out deleted ones:

<Tabs items={['Node', 'Python', 'Go', 'PHP']}>
<Tab value="Node">

```ts
const videos = await clipmux.assets.findByPassthrough('lesson_42')
const latest = videos[0]
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">

```python
res = requests.get(
    f"{os.environ['CLIPMUX_URL']}/v1/assets",
    params={"passthrough": "lesson_42"},
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['CLIPMUX_API_KEY']}"},
)
videos = res.json()["data"]
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Go">

```go
u := os.Getenv("CLIPMUX_URL") + "/v1/assets?passthrough=" + url.QueryEscape("lesson_42")
req, _ := http.NewRequest("GET", u, nil)
req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+os.Getenv("CLIPMUX_API_KEY"))
// the response's "data" is the list, newest first
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="PHP">

```php
$ch = curl_init(getenv('CLIPMUX_URL') . '/v1/assets?passthrough=' . urlencode('lesson_42'));
curl_setopt_array($ch, [
    CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
    CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => ['Authorization: Bearer ' . getenv('CLIPMUX_API_KEY')],
]);
$videos = json_decode(curl_exec($ch), true)['data'];
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

This needs `assets:read`. Use it to repair a record that missed its
webhooks, or to check before creating a second upload for the same record.

## Check it works

Upload a test file with a passthrough, then look it up:

```bash
npx @clipmux/node upload sample.mp4 --passthrough lesson_42
curl -s "https://video.example.com/v1/assets?passthrough=lesson_42" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLIPMUX_API_KEY" | jq '.data[] | {id, status, passthrough}'
```

The new video is first in the list. An empty list means the passthrough was
spelled differently, or the key belongs to another app: each app sees only
its own videos.
